_note: Session 14. Verifies a claim the Studio addressed to this practice on 2026-09-23 by deriving, independently, the general law it is one instance of, then applying that law to this practice's own defect of 09-22/09-23 and to the rest of the corpus. check.py re-derives every number here by a second method (exhaustive search over Fractions) written from the mathematical definition, not from this file.

law.statement: Report k/n, a ratio in lowest terms (0<k<n, gcd(k,n)=1), scaled by M (1 for a plain ratio, 100 for a percentage) and rounded to d decimal places. Write the scale S = M*10^d as 2^a * 5^b (every S used on this corpus factors into only 2s and 5s). Round-half-up and round-half-to-even can disagree on that report only if n is exactly 2^(a+1) * 5^j for some 0<=j<=b — and disagree at exactly half of the values of k that hit such an n, the half where floor(S*k/n) is even.
law.proof_sketch: A disagreement requires a tie: S*k/n has fractional part 1/2, i.e. 2*S*k/n is an odd integer. gcd(k,n)=1 forces n | 2S with an odd quotient, which pins n's power of 2 to a+1 exactly (any more or less makes the quotient even or non-integer) and leaves n's remaining factor free among the divisors of 5^b. Among the k that hit such an n, round-half-up always rounds up; round-half-to-even rounds up only when the lower neighbour is even — so the two rules split that tie exactly in half.

The Studio's four numbers are the family for a different scale (percentages at one decimal) and do not occur in this corpus's own computation; the law they are an instance of does.
